# Coastline (measure-feature) build

The coastline drawn on the map AND used to eliminate stations for the
"how far from the coastline" question is generated by
`scripts/build_measure_features.py` (function `build_coastline`) into
`src/data/measure-features.geojson.json` (features with `properties.key == "coastline"`).

## How it works (the pipeline that finally worked)

1. **Source = OSM `natural=coastline`** (`scripts/measure_src/osm_coastline_bayarea.geojson`),
   the exact line the CARTO basemap draws, so our shore lands on the real coast
   (the old Census water-mask approach sat ~25–40 m inland — do NOT go back to it).
   `linemerge(unary_union(...))` stitches the ~850 raw ways into continuous lines.

2. **Dams** (`cfg["dams"]`, list of `[[lon,lat],[lon,lat]]` bank-to-bank pairs).
   For each, snap both banks to the nearest point on the merged coastline
   (reject if >0.006° ≈ 660 m off — that mouth isn't traced by OSM there), then
   build a straight **wall** line extended 0.0006° past each bank.

3. **Polygonize** `lines + dam walls + clip.exterior` into faces. The open bay is
   `max(faces, key=lambda f: f.intersection(saltwater).area)` (the face with the
   most saltwater-mask overlap — a rep-point-in-mask test is UNRELIABLE because
   far-offshore rep points fall outside the Census water polygon). `bayface.boundary`
   is the shore. Sealed sloughs/estuaries and the **marsh islets inside them**
   become separate faces and vanish automatically; real bay islands (Angel,
   Treasure/Yerba Buena, Alcatraz) come back as holes and are kept.

4. **Clip to play area**: `shore.intersection(play.buffer(0.004))`. Keep it small —
   this keeps every real in-play shore INCLUDING shoreline parks that are not
   census places (e.g. Point Pinole). Do NOT clip on `play.difference(bayface)`
   ("in-play land"): it wrongly drops park shores and, where near-shore water
   isn't part of the main bay face, wrongly keeps out-of-play shore.

5. **Region excludes** (`cfg["coast_exclude"]`, list of `[w,s,e,n]` bboxes),
   applied as `shore.difference(box)`. Used for coast that must be dropped but
   can't be told apart topologically:
   - Suisun Bay + Delta (east of Carquinez Strait neck)
   - San Pablo Bay north of the 38.0021 cutoff
   - **Out-of-play Marin/North-Bay shore** (Tiburon/Sausalito/Richardson Bay,
     San Rafael/San Quentin). Marin is ONE continuous landmass with the in-play
     East Bay (they join around the top of the bbox), so polygonize can't separate
     it. Two boxes shaped to spare **Angel Island** (lon -122.446..-122.418, lat
     up to 37.872): `[-122.70, 37.873, -122.43, 38.0021]` (north of Raccoon Strait;
     east edge -122.43 keeps Point Molate/San Pablo) and
     `[-122.70, 37.820, -122.448, 37.873]` (west of Angel).

6. **Simplify** to `cfg` detail 0.00015° (~17 m, the level Andrew picked) and
   drop fragments shorter than 0.003°.

## Adding / fixing a mouth
- Andrew sends bank-to-bank coords as `lat, lon, lat, lon` (per mouth). Convert to
  `[[lon,lat],[lon,lat]]` and append to `cfg["dams"]` with a comment naming the spot.
- If a stretch traces up a creek or shows a marsh ring, it needs a dam across the
  mouth. If a whole region is out of play, add a `coast_exclude` box instead
  (shape it to spare any in-play island nearby).

## Verify before pushing
- Rebuild: `cd <repo> && CITY=bayarea python scripts/build_measure_features.py`
- Check specific regions by summing `LineString.intersection(box).length` over the
  `key=="coastline"` features (out-of-play regions → 0; in-play shores → >0;
  nothing north of 38.0021).
- Render red-line PNGs of the changed area with matplotlib to eyeball vs. the map.
- `npm run lint && npm run test && npm run build` (147 tests must pass; the
  measureFeatureShading / questionRegions tests consume this file).
- Do NOT commit the throwaway `scripts/_*.py` debug/render scripts.

## Delivery
Commit `scripts/build_measure_features.py` + `src/data/measure-features.geojson.json`
to the feature branch and push (see repo knowledge for the PAT remote). Preview:
https://andrewku123.github.io/jetlagapp/pr-preview/pr-<N>/ (hard-refresh ~2 min).
